title: Descent of one section to the sum of its sheet coordinates
statement: Use the trace data [def-sfb-finite-etale-trace-data]. For a finite etale p:V→S, a rational continuous-coefficient module sheaf L and a section s of p*L over B×_S V, there is a unique r∈L(B) with this property: on any C→B mapping to an etale U→S with a finite splitting σ, if the restriction of s has sheet coordinates t_j∈L(C) under the canonical sheet units, then r restricts to the sum of the t_j. This asserts descent of a single section; it contains no linearity, module morphism, or integral-image claim.

proof.text: Use the bijective sheet units to obtain unique sheet coordinates. The adjunction unit is natural, so these coordinates commute with restriction.

Apply the source-library finite-etale splitting-cover theorem to the identity etale object over S. Convert its explicit clopen splitting data into TraceImageSplitting: each supplied inverse identifies its summand with the base, and the pullback universal property identifies the resulting section with the canonical sheet lift. The continuous inclusion of the small etale site pushes the covering sieve to a pro-etale covering sieve. Pull it back to B. Consequently the presieve of all arrows C→B whose domain maps to an etale splitting object is covering.

On an overlap, use the coproduct presentations of the pulled-back sheets. The local-permutation lemma gives an open cover and a fixed bijection of the two sheet sets on each open. Corresponding sheet maps agree, hence their coordinates agree by sheet-unit injectivity. Reindex the finite sum. Separatedness gives equality on the overlap. The empty case is the empty-cover sheaf axiom.

For every arrow of this presieve the sum is uniquely characterized by all splittings of its domain, by the preceding independence result. Choose this unique value, obtaining a family. Naturality of coordinates and equality of the two composite restriction maps prove compatibility. The sheaf axiom glues the family. Every arrow appearing in the required formula belongs to this same presieve, so the gluing equation proves the formula directly. Bijectivity of sheet units identifies arbitrary supplied coordinates with the chosen ones. Uniqueness of the amalgamation proves the required uniqueness. No module linearity or integral image is used.

proof_origin.place: Completed S2 Lean proof: natural sheet coordinates, universal finite coproduct base change, local permutation comparison, source splitting-cover conversion, and sheaf amalgamation on the presieve of all split domains.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteEtaleTrace_section_sum_descent
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {V S : Scheme.{u}} (p : V ⟶ S) [IsFinite p] [Etale p]
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (traceFieldRing l E S))
    (B : S.ProEt)
    (s : ((traceModulePullback l E p).obj L).val.obj
      (op (AsSmall.up.obj ((proEtaleBaseChange p).obj B)))) :
    ∃! r : L.val.obj (op (AsSmall.up.obj B)),
      ∀ (U : S.ProEt) (_ : Etale U.hom) (J : Type u) [Fintype J]
        (σ : TraceImageSplitting p U J) (C : S.ProEt) (a : C ⟶ B) (h : C ⟶ U)
        (t : J → L.val.obj (op (AsSmall.up.obj C))),
        (∀ j, traceImageSheetRestriction σ h j ((traceModulePullback l E p).obj L)
          (((traceModulePullback l E p).obj L).val.map
            (AsSmall.up.map ((proEtaleBaseChange p).map a)).op s) =
              traceImageSheetUnit l E p L σ h j (t j)) →
          L.val.map (AsSmall.up.map a).op r = ∑ j, t j
